brief: Morgan Stanley's 2027 global outlook argues growth stays resilient because AI capex and wealth effects offset energy-driven inflation and tighter policy. Baseline: Fed hikes to 4.25-4.5% by 1Q27 and holds through 2027 before cutting by 2Q28; ECB to 3%, BoJ to 1.75%, both similarly timed; EM diverges, with India hiking to 6.25% while Brazil and Mexico ease. AI investment (equity-analyst capex forecasts of $1.6tn in 2027, $1.8tn in 2028) is the swing factor for both growth and US tax receipts, and analysts have not cut those numbers despite US mid-term election uncertainty, though 5GW of capacity shifted from 2028 to 2029. Four alternative scenarios test that baseline: aggregate-demand overheating forces the Fed to 5.625% as unemployment falls to 3.5%; faster AI productivity lifts growth without inflation, holding the Fed at 4.375%; an AI investment pullback cuts US growth near 1%, pushing unemployment above 5% and the Fed down to 1.375%; and a Gulf-driven oil shock to $125-150/bbl forces the Fed to 5.125%, tipping a mild 2027 recession before cuts resume by end-2028.
